node-1.label: The patient has had a 4-month history of bilateral groin pain and right buttock pain, with the right hip more painful than the left.

node-2.label: The patient was a 41-year-old Japanese woman with a medical history of iron-deficiency anemia diagnosed 2 years earlier and current iron supplement use; she had no history of trauma, alcohol abuse, or steroid use, and no previous fractures including fragility fractures.

node-3.label: Her height was 155 cm, weight 42 kg, and BMI 18.7 kg/m2; she could walk for about 10 minutes without assistance at a slow pace.

node-4.label: Passive motion of both hip joints was limited (flexion 100°, internal rotation 5°, external rotation 15°, abduction 20° on both sides); straight-leg raise of the right limb caused significant pain; neurovascular status of both lower extremities was normal; according to the Japanese Orthopaedic Association hip-joint function score, the right hip was 46/100 and the left hip was 56/100 (comprising 40 points for pain, 20 for range of motion, 20 for walking, and 20 for activities of daily living).

attrs.why: New radiologist analysis continues to support bilateral hip OA/dysplasia as the leading diagnosis at 0.75: chronic bilateral groin pain, limited passive hip motion, positive right SLR, and low JOA hip scores. Although MRI subchondral T1 low-signal line/STIR hyperintensity and low femoral-neck BMD raise AVN/insufficiency fracture/osteoporosis, the absence of trauma, steroid/alcohol use, and prior fractures, plus no systemic inflammatory signs, leaves OA/dysplasia most probable.

Normal CRP and absence of systemic signs lower the likelihood of inflammatory arthritis. Bilateral joint involvement and limited ROM remain weakly supportive, but ESR/RF/anti-CCP are unavailable. Confidence decreased from 0.15 to 0.08.

MRI subchondral T1 low-signal line and STIR hyperintensity are characteristic of avascular necrosis, increasing concern. However, absent trauma, steroid/alcohol use, and prior fractures argue against classic AVN, so confidence rises only from 0.05 to 0.15.
Right buttock pain and positive SLR could suggest radiculopathy; normal neuro and limited passive hip ROM refute

node-9.label: MRI of the hips shows a subchondral T1 low-signal line and STIR hyperintensity.

node-10.label: Bone mineral density is low at the femoral neck.

node-12.label: Osteoporosis-related subchondral insufficiency fracture of the hip

attrs.why: MRI subchondral T1 low-signal line and STIR hyperintensity, together with low femoral-neck BMD and normal CRP, suggest an osteoporosis-related subchondral insufficiency fracture. The absence of trauma/steroids is compatible with insufficiency fracture rather than classic AVN. Hip X-ray and bone turnover markers are unavailable, so confidence is 0.25.
